title: Blackout rehearsal: tiered load-shedding, circuit-breaker validation, and atomic restore certification
creator: Priya Shah
description: Objective: Validate end-to-end behavior of an active-passive evacuation where the primary region experiences a sudden blackout. Exercise tiered load-shedding, per-route circuit-breakers, and an atomic restore from KV snapshots while preserving SLOs for high-priority customers. This drill focuses on: 1) exercising automated circuit breakers and policy escalations, 2) proving KV snapshot restore produces consistent model-serving state, 3) exercising rollback and progressive traffic ramp-down/up, and 4) collecting signals to update runbooks and tuning guidance.
success_criteria: 1) High-priority routes remain within SLOs (p95 latency < 200ms for host-tier-1) during and after failover. 2) KV and tokenstore consistency checks report zero divergence for pinned model versions and session state within 5 minutes of completion. 3) Circuit-breaker thresholds trip at expected loads and recover according to policy. 4) Restore validation harness verifies data integrity and checksums. 5) Post-drill action items created and owners assigned.
preconditions:
- Backup snapshots for tokenstore/KV taken within last 15 minutes before rehearsal window.
- DR ops team on-call assigned and paged.
- Canary traffic generator configured to simulate tiered customer mixes.
- Monitoring dashboards and SLO alerts are enabled and annotated.
- A non-production but production-like cluster and a dedicated test customer org are reserved for the exercise.

runbook_steps:
Phase 0 - Preparation:
1) Confirm snapshots exist and are uploaded to s3://redwood-dr-snapshots/2026-03-13/ENG-59713.
2) Notify observability and support teams; set experiment tags in datadog:drill=ENG-59713.
3) Start canary traffic generator with baseline profile and capture baseline metrics for 10m.

Phase 1 - Simulated Blackout:
4) Trigger failover: use orchestration playbook 'failover/trigger_active_passive.sh --target passive-region=eu-west-1 --reason=simulated-blackout --tag=ENG-59713'.
5) Immediately raise global circuit-breakers to tiered thresholds: invoke admin API /admin/v1/circuit-breakers with payload to set p95-latency cutoff and request-per-second caps.
6) Monitor for automatic routing: ensure smart-routing redirects eligible requests to eu-west-1 and that fallback model variants are used for low-tier plans.

Phase 2 - Load-shedding and CB Verification:
7) Ramp canary traffic by +3x in 2 minutes and observe which routes get shed. Verify that shed order follows priority map (free -> standard -> enterprise).
8) Validate circuit-breaker trip metrics and log events in /metrics/cb-trips. Expected: 5-10 trips among low-tier routes, zero for enterprise.

Phase 3 - Atomic Restore and KV Validation:
9) After failover stabilizes, perform atomic restore from snapshot: 'restore/atomic_restore --snapshot s3://redwood-dr-snapshots/... --target eu-west-1 --dry-run=false'.
10) Run data-integrity check: 'validation/kv_consistency_check --left active-kv --right restored-kv --allowed-drift=0'.
11) Run session replay tests for long-lived sessions and streaming reconnect tests.

Phase 4 - Rollback and Cleanup:
12) If restore fails checks, initiate rollback to snapshot pre-state and re-run restore with alternate snapshot.
13) Gradually lower circuit-breaker thresholds and ramp traffic back to normal patterns in 30m windows.
14) Terminate canary traffic and mark experiment complete.
validation_checks:
- SLO dashboard: runtime/slo/host-tier-1 shows p95 < 200ms.
- KV checksums match: sha256(restored) == sha256(snapshot)
- Tokenstore session replay success rate >= 99%
- No unhandled 5xx spikes > 2% sustained for > 5m
- Audit logs contain explicit restore command and actor IDs
rollback_plan:
If critical validation fails (data mismatch, >5% 5xxs, or enterprise SLO breach):
1) Pause traffic routing to passive region.
2) Revert to last-known-good snapshot using restore/atomic_restore --snapshot s3://redwood-dr-snapshots/last-known-good.
3) Use emergency routing policy to send traffic to warm standby in us-east-1.
4) Open a Sev with postmortem owner and start forensic capture for at least 24h.

- Tune circuit-breaker thresholds based on observed trip distribution.
- Update SLO runbook with improved canary profiles and allowed-drift values.
- Schedule follow-up drill focused on cold-start latency in 4 weeks.
notes:
Design decision: prefer atomic snapshot restore to avoid partial state that confuses model-serving runtime. Trade-off: atomic restores can take longer and increase initial latency during reintegration; mitigations include progressive traffic ramping and serving degraded model variants.
We will use a reserved non-prod account that mirrors customer auth to avoid exposing production customer data. KMS keys for snapshots are accessible to DR engineers via temporary role for the exercise.
